content: Teplizumab has been approved as a pharmacologic intervention to delay the onset of stage 3 type 1 diabetes in individuals aged 8 years and older who are at high risk for developing the disease. This approval is based on evidence from clinical studies demonstrating that teplizumab can slow the progression to symptomatic diabetes. In a clinical trial involving high-risk individuals, participants were divided into two groups: one group received teplizumab, while the other group received a placebo. The results showed that a significant proportion of individuals who received teplizumab (43%) were able to delay the onset of diabetes, compared to 72% of individuals in the placebo group who progressed to symptomatic diabetes. Teplizumab is particularly effective in individuals who are antibody-positive and lack the HLA-DR4 genetic marker. However, common side effects associated with teplizumab include rash, which occurred in 73% of participants, and lymphopenia, a reduction in lymphocyte count.
